title: SLO Credit Exchange and Capacity Hedging Playbook
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview:

This document defines the SLO Credit Exchange concept and the operational playbook for converting error budget into transferable credits, automated hedging, and the internal marketplace used to move reliability headroom between services. The goal is to make reliability trade-offs explicit, auditable, and automatable so teams can respond to transient demand without costly manual provisioning.

Intended audience:
- Platform SREs and service on-call engineers.
- Product and feature owners who own SLOs.
- Capacity planning and engineering finance.

Terminology (concise):
- SLO Credit: an internal unit representing a portion of a monthly error budget for a named service.
- Wallet: ledger entry per service with current credits and obligations.
- Order: programmatic request to buy, sell, or borrow credits.
- Hedging: automated conversion of credits to capacity reservations or token-priority adjustments.

Why this model:
1) Quantifies reliability as a scarce resource that teams can manage like budget.
2) Enables rapid, governed capacity movement during demand spikes.
3) Produces auditable traces of reliability interventions for post-incident analysis.

Roles and ownership:
- Platform SRE: marketplace operator and incident owner for marketplace availability. Contact: ops-marketplace@redwood.
- Service Owner: maintains SLOs and approves purchases when policy requires.
- Capacity Planning / Eng-Finance: sets baseline pricing and maps credits to reserved capacity commitments.
- On-call: responsible for runbook execution when alerts trigger automated loans or hedges.

Operational model summary:
- Mapping: each service maps its SLO to a wallet with N credits. Example mapping rules will be stored in the credit conversion catalog.
- Order types: spot-buy, reserved-buy, emergency-loan. Each type has TTL, price, and operational obligations.
- Governance: three profiles (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) govern auto-approve thresholds and pricing multipliers.

Pricing and conversion example (illustrative):
- Baseline SLO: monthly availability target 99.9% (error budget 0.1%).
- 1 credit = 0.01% monthly error budget. Thus monthly wallet size 10 credits.
- Conversion table sets region-specific capacity equivalence. Example: 1 credit -> 0.5 GPU-hours in us-west-2 (subject to weekly update).

Marketplace lifecycle flows:
1) Buy flow (auto-approve case):
   a) Service submits order via CLI or UI: command form is rdm market buy --service SERVICE --credits N --type TYPE --max-price P
   b) Marketplace checks wallet caps and governance profile and either executes or routes for approval.
   c) On success, wallet balance updates and an autoscaler hook is invoked to create capacity reservations if required.

2) Emergency loan flow (fast hedge):
   a) Trigger: SLO burn rate exceeds configured threshold (for example: 20% of monthly budget consumed within 1 hour).
   b) Marketplace auto-issues an emergency loan up to configured limit and invokes hedging automations to reserve hot pool capacity.
   c) If loan repayment conditions are violated, automated throttle policies and repayment enforcement run.

Monitoring and alerts (what to watch):
- Wallet balance by service (gauge).
- SLO burn-rate short window (1h) and medium window (24h).
- Marketplace open orders and loan default rate.
- Hot pool utilization across regions.

Alert examples and immediate actions:
- MARKETPLACE_LOW_CREDIT: trigger when wallet balance <= 2 for critical service. Action: notify service owner and Platform SRE; allow quick purchase link in alert.
- SLO_FAST_BURN: trigger when short-window burn exceeds 20% of monthly. Action: attempt auto-loan, page on-call, and start triage runbook below.
- LOAN_OVERDUE: loan TTL exceeded. Action: enforce throttles for non-critical tokens, notify finance, and open a repayment incident.

Triage and runbook (SLO_FAST_BURN) 
1) Triage (0-10 minutes):
   - Confirm alert validity: check telemetry for request rates, error spikes, recent deploys.
   - Run quick trace sampling to find error signatures.
2) Immediate mitigation (10-30 minutes):
   - If auto-loan was issued, verify hot-pool reservation and capacity warming.
   - If no auto-loan, consider manual purchase: rdm market buy --service SERVICE --credits N --type emergency-loan --max-price P
   - If capacity appears healthy but errors persist, roll back the suspect deploy per deployment rollback procedure.
3) Containment (30-90 minutes):
   - Apply token-priority throttles for non-critical tenants to preserve wallet. Command form: rdm token throttle --service SERVICE --policy POLICY_NAME
   - Coordinate with product owner for feature flag gating or reduced concurrency.
4) Recovery and close (post-stable):
   - Ensure wallet ledger entries are documented and exported for the incident.
   - If loan > threshold or repayment overdue, schedule post-incident review with involved parties.

Automations and integration points:
- Autoscaler hook: marketplace posts reservation requests to internal provisioning API. The autoscaler creates ephemeral hot pool instances and reports back with allocation IDs.
- Token-priority controller: reads wallet balance and governance profile to compute soft priorities for request admission.
- Audit exports: monthly ledger export available via CLI and delivered to the finance S3 bucket.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Marketplace service outage: fail-open for non-emergency purchases; fail-closed for emergency loans. Maintain a warm backup region with a read-only ledger replica for manual reconciliation.
- Double-spend or balance mismatch: ledger is persisted to a strongly-consistent store. Reconciliation job command: rdm market reconcile --since DATE. Discrepancies create an evidence bundle for SRE review.

Governance and policies:
- Auto-approve thresholds by governance profile: Conservative (max auto-approve 10% of wallet), Balanced (20%), Aggressive (50%).
- Approval flows for non-auto orders: require approver set consisting of service owner and a capacity planning rep. Approvals recorded in the ledger with timestamp and approver id.

Implementation checklist (MVP):
- Marketplace API endpoints and idempotent order processing.
- CLI: rdm market buy/sell/loan/export/reconcile.
- Grafana dashboards and alerting rules for wallet and burn metrics.
- Autoscaler integration hook and token-priority controller.
- Monthly audit export automation to S3 for finance.

Security and retention:
- Ledger access via RBAC. Only Platform SRE, finance, and service owners have write access.
- Retain audit records for seven years. Emergency loan metadata marked for restricted access for 90 days following issuance.

Open questions and next actions:
- Decide whether internal credit pricing should be pegged to live spot prices or stable reserved rates. Action owner: Capacity Planning. Due: 2026-03-01.
- Define interactions with Dedicated customer guarantees; coordinate with Legal. Action owner: Enterprise PM + Legal. Due: 2026-02-28.
